commitments.ndc_target: Enhanced NDC (2022): 31.89% unconditional and 43.20% conditional GHG reduction from business-as-usual by 2030; FOLU Net Sink 2030 for the forestry sector
key_laws: Law No. 32/2009 on Environmental Protection and Management
Job Creation Law / Omnibus Law (2020, revised 2023) — weakened environmental permitting, controversial
Presidential Regulation 112/2022 on Accelerating Renewable Energy Development
Indonesia FOLU Net Sink 2030 Operational Plan (2022)
Moratorium on new primary forest and peatland conversion — made permanent 2019

climate.rationale: Indonesia is the world's 7th-largest emitter once LULUCF is included, with coal still providing 61% of electricity and new captive coal plants being built to power nickel smelters for the EV supply chain. The $20B Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) signed 2022 has delivered limited concessional finance and no firm coal retirement schedule. CAT rates overall policies 'Critically insufficient' — the weakest G20 category.

forests_land.rationale: Primary forest loss has fallen sharply from the 2016 peak — 2024 saw the lowest deforestation in two decades per Global Forest Watch — but 2025 data show a rebound driven by palm oil, pulpwood, and nickel mining concessions. Peatland drainage and fires remain a structural risk: Indonesia holds ~36% of the world's tropical peat carbon. The permanent moratorium on new primary-forest and peatland conversion (2019) is real progress, but enforcement on existing concessions is patchy.

biodiversity.rationale: One of the world's most biodiverse countries, hosting Sumatran orangutans, Javan rhinos (fewer than 80 left), Sumatran tigers (~400), and the heart of the Coral Triangle. IUCN Red List shows accelerating declines: the Tapanuli orangutan (described 2017) already critically endangered, Javan rhino population hit by poaching in 2023–2024. Illegal wildlife trade and habitat fragmentation are the dominant drivers. [Planet Lens v1.1] Score = 80% Biodiversity Intactness Index (58.0%, NHM 2020, area-weighted) + 20% Red List Index (0.75, IUCN/OWID 2024).

protected_areas.rationale: Terrestrial protected areas at ~12.2% and marine at ~3.1% (Protected Planet), both well below the GBF 30×30 target. Government pledged to expand marine protected areas to 30% by 2045 — a decade later than the global target. Coral Triangle reefs, among the planet's most species-rich marine ecosystems, remain under-protected and exposed to destructive fishing.

pollution.rationale: Jakarta routinely ranks among the world's most polluted major cities, with annual PM2.5 around 40 µg/m³ (8× WHO guideline). Peatland fires during dry years send transboundary haze across Southeast Asia. Plastic leakage into the ocean is among the highest globally; rivers in Java are heavily contaminated with textile and industrial effluent.

agriculture.rationale: Palm oil is the defining commodity — Indonesia supplies ~59% of global output — with a mixed record on the ISPO/RSPO sustainability certifications and continued links to deforestation. Rice paddies are a major methane source (part of the 8% agriculture share). Smallholder yields lag regional peers, and pesticide and fertilizer overuse are documented in Java and Sumatra.

env_governance.rationale: Environmental governance has weakened under the 2020 Omnibus Law, which loosened environmental-impact-assessment requirements and centralized permit authority. Global Witness recorded 4 environmental defenders killed in 2024 and documented escalating criminalization of activists opposing nickel, coal, and palm projects. The Prabowo administration (inaugurated October 2024) has accelerated strategic-project exemptions and downplayed JETP climate conditionality.

recent_actions.action: Prabowo government signalled it may exit or renegotiate the $20B JETP framework, citing dissatisfaction with the ratio of grants vs loans and conditionality on coal retirement
Indonesia inaugurated first phase of Nusantara (IKN) capital relocation in East Kalimantan — environmental impact contested; 256,000 ha concession overlaps peatland and orangutan habitat
Launched expanded mangrove rehabilitation program targeting 600,000 ha by 2030 under FOLU Net Sink plan
Approved 21 GW of new captive coal capacity in nickel/aluminium industrial parks (Sulawesi, North Maluku) outside JETP restrictions
Constitutional Court ruled in favour of Indigenous groups in a forest-tenure case, ordering formal recognition of 1.2 million ha of adat (customary) forest
Ministry of Environment and Forestry merged with upstream Ministry of Energy oversight under Prabowo restructuring, raising concerns about independent environmental review

context.key_tension: Indonesia is being asked to protect the world's third-largest rainforest and third-largest tropical peat store while simultaneously becoming the electric-vehicle supply chain's nickel backbone — an export boom now powered by captive coal that sits outside its headline climate pledges.
